NVDA.text: Nvidia jumped about 11.6%, far outpacing the Nasdaq, as SpaceX said it would standardize on Nvidia’s Vera Rubin architecture and renewed hyperscaler capex commitments reinforced confidence that AI-compute demand remains exceptionally strong.

AVGO.text: Broadcom rose about 9.9%, mostly with the resurgent AI-chip complex as hyperscaler spending and Nvidia’s SpaceX/Vera Rubin endorsement reinforced data-center demand; no distinct Broadcom operating catalyst was confirmed, and the EU antitrust document ruling was a headwind rather than the driver.

TSM.text: TSM gained about 3.9%, largely with the AI-semiconductor rebound rather than on new company news; Nvidia-led strength and renewed hyperscaler spending lifted chip names, while TSMC’s next monthly sales release was not due until August 10.

ASML.text: ASML rose about 6.9%, mostly with the AI-semiconductor rebound as renewed hyperscaler spending supported advanced-chip demand; no new ASML-specific catalyst was confirmed, so the move appears more sector-led than company-led.

DDOG.text: Datadog fell about 12.7% after earnings because, despite beating consensus and raising guidance, its revenue beat narrowed versus the prior quarter and Q3 implied only modest sequential growth, disappointing the elevated expectations embedded in the stock.

META.text: Meta rebounded about 6.4%, roughly in line with the Nasdaq’s 5.2% weekly gain, with no confirmed new company-specific catalyst; lower yields after a weak jobs report and renewed risk appetite in megacap tech appear to have been the main support.

PLTR.text: Palantir surged about 39.8%, its best week since 2024, after Q2 revenue grew 93% and U.S. commercial revenue jumped 149% while management raised its 2026 U.S. commercial outlook, making the move overwhelmingly company-specific.

SPCX.text: SpaceX rose about 22.8% as strong first public-quarter results—$7.8 billion of revenue and $3.5 billion of adjusted EBITDA—helped shares overcome midweek fears about heavy AI spending and the lockup expiration; Friday’s 15.8% jump came as feared insider selling failed to materialize.

MU.text: Micron gained about 6.6% despite late-week memory-sector weakness, with the rebound supported by persistent AI-driven DRAM/HBM tightness; Friday’s SK Hynix fab-expansion news trimmed gains, but analysts noted the added supply will take years to arrive.
